thoughts.content:
RCA Conclusion — HighErrorRate, shop/frontend

Classification: CONFIRMED

Symptom verification (currently occurring)
loadgen pod (the traffic generator hitting the frontend) shows 100% failure, continuously, up to the current moment:
``
2026-10-02T20:25:27Z GET /api/items -> 502
... (every single request through 20:26:05Z) -> 502
`
This exactly matches the alert: "100% of requests to /api/ returned 5xx over the last 5 minutes." Both frontend nginx pods (dgg8q, ktzwl) corroborate with identical, uninterrupted 502 responses and nginx error log entries:
`
connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream,
request: "GET /api/items HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.96.190.97:8080/items", host: "frontend"
`

Root cause
The api Service's targetPort does not match the container port the api Deployment actually listens on.

kubectl get svc api -n shop -o yaml → live spec: port: 8080, targetPort: 9090, endpoints: 10.244.1.131:9090,10.244.2.124:9090
kubectl get deploy api -n shop -o yaml → container ports: [{containerPort: 8080}], readiness/liveness probes target port 8080, and app log confirms api listening on :8080
Nothing in either api pod listens on 9090 → every connection kube-proxy DNATs to podIP:9090 is refused at the pod → nginx surfaces this as 502.

Evidence this is a drift, not original design: the Service's own kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation records the originally applied spec as {"ports":[{"port":8080,"targetPort":8080}]} — i.e., it was deployed correctly with targetPort: 8080. The live spec.ports[0].targetPort is now 9090, diverging from the declared/applied config. Something patched/edited the Service object directly after creation, redirecting all traffic to a port nothing listens on.

Ruled out
Node health: all 3 nodes Ready (get nodes -o wide).
Resource exhaustion: kubectl top pods -n shop shows trivial usage (api: 1-2m CPU / 11-14Mi mem; frontend: 1m/7Mi) — not resource-related.
App/container crash: 0 restarts
